desc: Video game publisher and developer owning franchises such as Darksiders, Titan Quest, Gothic, Destroy All Humans and the SpongeBob games.
markets: Sells games to PC and console players; part of Embracer Group, formerly Nordic Games until renamed in 2016.
rationale: Gaming publisher with moderate brand awareness; F1 game and entertainment audience overlap exists, though Embracer controls marketing spend.
changed: Renamed from Nordic Games in 2016

name: Vlocity
desc: Former software company building industry-specific cloud applications on Salesforce for communications, media, energy, insurance, health and public sector customers.
markets: Sold subscriptions to large enterprises; now part of Salesforce as Salesforce Industries.
rationale: Brand absorbed into Salesforce, an F1 partner, so no standalone sponsorship case.
changed: Acquired by Salesforce in 2020
f1: Parent Salesforce is an F1 partner

name: Workday Adaptive Planning
desc: Cloud financial planning and analytics software, formerly Adaptive Insights, selling budgeting, forecasting and reporting tools to finance teams.
markets: Sold worldwide as part of Workday, which acquired Adaptive Insights in 2018.
rationale: Product of Workday, an existing F1 partner, so activation would run through the parent.
changed: Acquired by Workday in 2018 as Adaptive Insights
f1: Parent Workday is an F1 partner

name: Forcepoint
desc: Cybersecurity company selling data security, secure web gateway and secure access service edge products to enterprises and governments.
markets: Customers in many countries across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; owned by private equity firm Francisco Partners.
rationale: Security rivals CrowdStrike, Zscaler, Cato Networks and Keeper already sponsor F1, so category fit and enterprise hospitality value are clear.
changed: Acquired from Raytheon by Francisco Partners in 2021

name: Bitglass
desc: Former cloud access security broker and secure access service edge provider protecting data across cloud apps and mobile devices.
markets: Sold to enterprises; technology now sits inside Forcepoint's product line after acquisition.
rationale: Brand absorbed into Forcepoint after acquisition; no standalone sponsorship case or marketing budget remains.
changed: Acquired by Forcepoint in 2021

name: Data.ai
desc: Mobile app and digital market analytics company, formerly App Annie, tracking downloads, revenue, usage and advertising for apps and games.
markets: Sold subscriptions to app publishers, brands and investors worldwide; merged into Sensor Tower after acquisition.
rationale: Brand merged into Sensor Tower after acquisition, so there is no standalone sponsorship case.
changed: Formerly App Annie; acquired by Sensor Tower in 2024

name: Dixa
desc: Customer service software whose cloud platform unifies calls, chat, email and messaging and uses AI to route and automate conversations.
markets: Danish vendor selling to mid-size and large customer service teams, mainly in Europe; wider footprint not confirmed.
rationale: Customer-service software rivals Genesys and Freshworks already sponsor F1; Dixa is smaller, so fit is plausible but budget-limited.

name: Gainsight
desc: Customer success software that helps subscription businesses track customer health, reduce churn and expand accounts.
markets: Sells to subscription businesses in North America and Europe; majority-owned by Vista Equity Partners.
rationale: B2B software brand with strong enterprise community and events culture; F1 hospitality could support customer events, though budget is moderate.
changed: Majority stake acquired by Vista Equity Partners in 2020

name: Golden Technology
desc: Big data service company in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China, categorised by Crunchbase under big data, blockchain and cloud services.
markets: Based in Shenzhen; customers and any international activity cannot be confirmed from the data given.
rationale: Little is confirmed about this company, so no F1 case can be made.

name: HashCash Consultants
desc: Software and blockchain technology company offering white-label crypto exchange software, wallet and custody services, payments and consulting.
markets: Palo Alto address with development operations in India; sells exchange technology to businesses.
rationale: Crypto exchange rivals such as Coinbase and Kraken sponsor F1, but HashCash is a small technology supplier with limited brand.

name: LeCloud
desc: Chinese cloud video and live streaming company offering hosting, content delivery and cloud services to media, sports and enterprise customers.
markets: Part of the LeEco ecosystem in China; customers are media, sports and enterprise clients, with no verified international activity.
rationale: Parent LeEco suffered a financial collapse and the unit's current status is unclear; streaming fits sport but evidence is weak.
changed: Parent LeEco fell into severe financial difficulty in 2017

name: Meetyou
desc: Women's health and lifestyle app group whose Meiyou app tracks periods, pregnancy and parenting, with community content, e-commerce and advertising.
markets: Chinese consumer app with a large user base in China; no verified international operations.
rationale: Consumer app with large Chinese audience but no international footprint; F1 has limited appeal for its core women's health users.

name: ROOBO
desc: Hardware and artificial intelligence company developing smart home and voice-interaction products, including smart speakers, children's AI robots and voice modules.
markets: Sells devices and AI technology from China; international sales not confirmed.
rationale: Chinese consumer-hardware and AI firm with limited global brand; F1 technology tie-in is plausible but evidence is thin.

name: Sonatype
desc: Software supply chain security company behind Nexus repository manager and Maven Central, scanning open-source components for vulnerabilities and licence risk.
markets: Developer and enterprise customers worldwide use Nexus and Maven Central; majority-owned by Vista Equity Partners.
rationale: Developer-security brand with technology-showcase value; security rivals 1Password and CrowdStrike sponsor F1, but budget is modest.
changed: Majority stake acquired by Vista Equity Partners in 2019

name: Agora.io
desc: Real-time engagement platform offering video, voice, live streaming and messaging APIs for social, gaming, education and telehealth apps.
markets: Founded in Shanghai in 2013 with a major presence in Santa Clara; Chinese and international customers.
rationale: Developer-facing technology brand with global customers; F1 live-video and fan-engagement angle fits, though little consumer visibility.

name: AInnovation
desc: Chinese artificial intelligence company providing AI products and solutions, including computer vision and industrial optimisation, for retail, manufacturing and finance.
markets: Customers are Chinese retail, manufacturing and finance firms; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Chinese B2B AI supplier listed in Hong Kong with domestic focus; limited consumer brand and weak F1 fit.

name: Route Mobile
desc: Cloud communications platform provider offering A2P SMS, voice, email, OTT messaging, RCS and fraud-prevention services to enterprises and mobile operators.
markets: Serves enterprises and mobile operators worldwide; Proximus Group holds a controlling stake through BICS.
rationale: B2B messaging supplier with global enterprise clients; F1 hospitality could help sales, but marketing is low-profile and parent-controlled.
changed: Controlling stake acquired by Proximus Group via BICS, 2023-24

name: WingArc1st
desc: Japanese business intelligence and data software company known for Dr.Sum and MotionBoard, plus the SVF report output family.
markets: Sells to large Japanese enterprises and public bodies; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Japanese B2B software firm with strong domestic IT-buyer recognition but no consumer profile; weak F1 fit.
changed: Taken private by Bain Capital in 2022

name: ABEJA
desc: Tokyo AI company developing deep learning and large language model platforms, including ABEJA Platform, mainly for retail, manufacturing and logistics.
markets: Customers are mainly Japanese retail, manufacturing and logistics firms; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Japanese enterprise AI vendor with domestic focus and small marketing budget; limited F1 case.

name: ION Geophysical Corporation
desc: Former provider of seismic data, software and equipment for oil and gas exploration, including marine seismic data libraries and software.
markets: Served oil and gas explorers; the company went through bankruptcy and its assets were sold.
rationale: Bankrupt oilfield technology supplier; no sponsorship prospect despite energy majors being in F1.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 in 2022

name: Namaste Technologies
desc: Online retailer of vaporizers, smoking accessories and related products, sold through websites in many countries.
markets: Sold through websites in many countries; it changed focus several times and ran into financial difficulties in the early 2020s.
rationale: Vaporizer and smoking-accessory retail is restricted category for F1 sponsorship, and the company had financial difficulties.

name: 24SevenOffice
desc: Cloud business software platform for accounting, CRM, invoicing, project and time tracking, payroll and email for small and mid-size businesses.
markets: Sold via partners and accountants in Norway, Sweden, the UK and other European markets.
rationale: Nordic small-business software firm with modest marketing budget and European focus; weak F1 fit.

name: Cipia
desc: Israeli computer-vision AI company providing in-cabin driver and occupant monitoring software and hardware, including fleet safety cameras.
markets: Supplies carmakers and fleets, helping them meet driver-safety rules in Europe and elsewhere; formerly Eyesight Technologies.
rationale: Automotive safety technology suits F1 technology showcase, but small B2B supplier with limited marketing budget.
changed: Renamed from Eyesight Technologies to Cipia

name: CY4GATE
desc: Italian cyber intelligence company offering digital intelligence platforms for law enforcement and intelligence agencies, plus cyber defence products and training.
markets: Customers are governments, defence bodies and large enterprises, mainly in Italy and Europe.
rationale: Government-focused intelligence supplier with no consumer profile; sensitive customer base makes F1 sponsorship unlikely.

name: ILOOKABOUT
desc: Canadian company known for online street-level imagery and geographic information tools for governments, utilities and commercial clients.
markets: Sells geospatial imagery to Canadian governments, utilities and commercial clients; no verified international activity.
rationale: Small geospatial data business with low brand awareness and limited marketing capacity; weak F1 fit.

name: NFON
desc: Cloud telephony and unified communications for small and mid-size businesses, with Cloudya and Nfon Business services sold through partners.
markets: Sells in Germany, Austria, Switzerland and other European countries through partners.
rationale: European SME telecom brand with modest marketing budget and regional focus; limited F1 case.

name: Remark Holdings
desc: AI and computer vision company with products such as KanKan facial recognition software, mostly sold in China.
markets: Products mostly sold in China from a Las Vegas base; persistent losses and going-concern warnings.
rationale: Small loss-making AI firm with facial-recognition controversy and no brand marketing capacity; poor F1 fit.

name: Verimatrix
desc: Security software providing app protection, DRM and anti-piracy tools for video and connected devices to pay-TV operators and streaming services.
markets: Customers include large telecoms and media groups worldwide; formerly Inside Secure, previously listed on Euronext Paris.
rationale: Anti-piracy supplier to streaming and pay-TV operators, relevant to F1 media rights, but B2B with little brand marketing.
changed: Formerly Inside Secure; delisted from Euronext Paris after change of ownership

name: Expert.ai
desc: Italian artificial intelligence company offering natural language processing and text analytics software with a hybrid symbolic and machine learning approach.
markets: Sells to insurance, banking, publishing and intelligence customers; formerly Expert System, listed on Euronext Growth Milan.
rationale: B2B language-AI vendor with limited consumer awareness; AI rivals sponsor F1, but expert.ai has a small marketing budget.
changed: Renamed from Expert System to expert.ai

name: Minim (formerly Zoom Telephonics)
desc: Maker of consumer internet access devices, including Motorola-branded cable modems and routers and Zoom-branded products, sold through retailers and online.
markets: Sold through retailers and online in North America; renamed Minim in 2021 after launching its Minim app.
rationale: Small consumer networking brand with North American retail focus and limited budget; F1 fit is weak.
changed: Renamed Minim in 2021

name: Salesloft
desc: Sales engagement and revenue orchestration software letting sales teams automate outreach, run cadences, track deals and forecast revenue using AI.
markets: Enterprise and mid-market sales teams; Vista Equity Partners-owned and combined with Clari.
rationale: B2B sales software with strong brand among sales leaders and event sponsorship experience; F1 hospitality suits client entertainment.
changed: Acquired by Vista Equity Partners in 2021; later combined with Clari

name: Ionic Security
desc: Data security company letting organisations share and use sensitive data by controlling access and encrypting information at the data level.
markets: Sells to enterprises, government and healthcare customers; no verified international expansion.
rationale: B2B security vendor with modest recognition; security rivals sponsor F1, but small budget limits fit.

name: Actual Experience
desc: UK company that sold AI-driven network analytics measuring application performance for end users so IT teams could find slowdown causes.
markets: Sold to enterprises and managed service providers; its parent was listed on London's AIM market.
rationale: Small UK network analytics vendor with little brand awareness; weak F1 fit.

name: Alimak Group
desc: Swedish industrial company supplying construction hoists, industrial elevators and platforms, with after-sales services, under Alimak, Manntech and Avanti brands.
markets: Customers are contractors, rental companies and industrial operators in more than 100 countries.
rationale: Global industrial B2B brand with no consumer profile; F1 hospitality could suit infrastructure clients, but little marketing use.
